pillar_reactions.evidence: Agreed without questions: 'Do you feel like, yeah, that is what I'm looking for? Yeah.' He had already accepted the premise before the pillar, having named over-training and lack of structure as his own problem.

Named it as the standout of the three and tied it to his own reasoning: 'the nutrition is really big for me because you could work out as much as, but if you're not eating right, it's like pointless, not pointless, but it's just a setback.' He also volunteered an advanced fasting practice unprompted: 'I do 24-hour fasts. I've gone up to a 45-hour fast at one point. I enjoy fasting, actually.'
Agreed with no clarifying questions and no pushback: 'no that sounds great that's amazing'. He did not probe the app, the video review loop or the Thursday live workout.

anchors.raw: And I do follow Trevor's workouts on YouTube. So I have been working with kettlebells for a few months now.
anchors.note: The strongest undercutting anchor in the batch and it belongs to the company. He has lost 20 lb and progressed from a 25 lb bell to 53 lb swings on free content alone, which is live proof that the free version works for him. Nobody repositioned against it.

Stated monthly surplus of roughly $2,000 after all expenses, surfaced by the rep in the last ten minutes. The rep observed 'Sounds like it is workable, right?' and then did not use it, moving instead to uncertainty framing.

anchors.raw: I have a lot of expenses right now. Like I said, my daughter's in therapy, so that's like a big issue for me right now too.
anchors.note: A committed family healthcare cost he raised twice, including as the reason he withdrew. This is the anchor that actually ended the buying conversation.

anchors.raw: I follow other trainers on YouTube that does Kettlebell and they offer programs, but I feel more with them. It's more of an email. They'll send you weekly workouts instead of actually paying attention and catering to each person one-on-one instead of having like a personal plan. It's more of a generic plan.
anchors.competitor: Other kettlebell coaches offering email-based programmes
anchors.note: He differentiated the one-to-one model himself and used it as his reason for taking the call. The clearest supportive anchor available and it was not built on.

unmet_demand.want: An affordable entry point given a stated blocker of cost and an unwillingness to take on another bill
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He was never shown the $200 a month community tier, which the same rep presented on four other calls in this batch when cost was the blocker. He was offered only third-party financing and instalments on the full $6,000. Whether the community would have suited him is untested.

unmet_demand.want: A periodised plan that stops him over-training, which he raised as his own risk
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer does serve this and the rep addressed it. Recorded only because it was his most specific stated need and it never became part of the value case at the point of price.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that a previously torn shoulder ligament can safely handle windmills and overhead lunges
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No clinical assessment exists in the programme. He raised stiffness and imbalance on exactly those two overhead movements and the answer was a general connective-tissue and mobility-routine claim.
